scoring_method: Manual review of each mode's final answer against the NASA article metadata and retrieved verification context in the source result file.

reference_facts.title: New two-metric theory of gravity with prior geometry
reference_facts.authors: Lightman, A. P., Lee, D. L.
reference_facts.publication: Physical Review D - Particles and Fields
reference_facts.main_context: The abstract describes a Lagrangian-based metric theory of gravity with three adjustable constants and two tensor fields, one of which is a nondynamic flat space metric eta.

mode_scores.notes: The answer makes a central false technical claim that the theory includes three adjustable constants and one tensor field, while the NASA record explicitly says three adjustable constants and two tensor fields. It also adds an unsupported causal phrasing around the post-Newtonian agreement. The tensor-field error is a major invented/contradicted claim in the main topic summary.

Most claims are grounded in the NASA record, including the title, authors, publication month/year, three adjustable constants, two tensor fields, eta, GRT post-Newtonian agreement, and six degrees of freedom. However, the final answer says gravitational waves travel null geodesics of the adjustable constant eta; the source says eta is a nondynamic flat space metric, not an adjustable constant. This is a factual distortion, but narrower than the direct answer's main tensor-field error.
